## Shared HTTP error behavior

Every HTTP operation registers the baseline `ErrorResponse` set 400, 403, 404, 409, 422, and 500. Route-specific statuses currently present across the surface are: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 422, 500, 503. FastAPI request validation runs before the handler and returns 422 with its validation-detail list. Existing `HTTPException` instances pass through unchanged, including handler-specific status codes and details.

The readiness route additionally declares 503 with `StudioReadinessResponse`, preserving dependency diagnostics when the service is alive but unavailable for traffic.

The shared handler guard maps uncaught exceptions as follows:

| Source exception | Status | Structured `detail.code` |
|---|---:|---|
| `FileNotFoundError, KeyError` | 404 | `not_found` |
| `PermissionError` | 403 | `forbidden` |
| `ValueError` | 422 | `invalid_request` |
| `RuntimeError` | 409 | `conflict` |
| `Exception` | 500 | `internal_error` |

A documented 400 schema is registered on every HTTP operation, but the shared guard has no generic 400 conversion. A handler must raise a 400 `HTTPException` explicitly for that response to occur.

## WebSocket routes

WebSockets do not register HTTP response models or the shared HTTP error schemas. The collaboration handler accepts a one-time invite token, emits a `session_snapshot`, accepts JSON object messages, broadcasts participant and editing events, treats `WebSocketDisconnect` as a normal disconnect, and always removes a joined participant in its cleanup path.

| Domain | Path | Handler | Handshake request | Response/error contract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| algorithm-lab | `/api/v2/algorithm-lab/session/{session_id}/collaborate` | `collaborate` | Path: `session_id`: `str` (required)<br>Query: `token`: `str` (required invite token) | JSON frames; no FastAPI response model or registered HTTP error schema |
